coverage_notes:
WHAT IS DOCUMENTED (14 people, all cited):
- Head coach: 1 (Erickson).
- On-field assistants: 9 (Bratkowski, Lubick, Smith, Arnold, Karmelowicz, Kehoe, Orgeron, Tuberville, Wood). This matches the full nine-assistant NCAA limit of the era and is corroborated by two independent sources (Wikipedia's season-page coaching-staff table and SB Nation/State of The U's 2022 retrospective written specifically about the 1991 staff).
- Strength & conditioning: 1 (Brad Roll), with a second corroborating source (USA S&C Coaches Hall of Fame bio).
- Graduate assistants: 3 (Randy Shannon, Jim Michalczik, Eddie Gran), each with two sources.

TIERS I COULD NOT RECOVER — no rows padded:
- Operations / personnel / recruiting (ops): ZERO documented. No "director of football operations," recruiting coordinator, or administrative-assistant name for 1991 Miami surfaced in any source I could reach. This role tier barely existed in 1991 college football and was not covered by online sources.
- Medical (athletic trainers, team physicians): ZERO documented. Miami's best-known head football athletic trainer of the period, Kevin O'Neill, left for the Dallas Cowboys with Jimmy Johnson after the 1988 season, so he was NOT on the 1991 staff; I found no name for his 1991 successor. Do not assume O'Neill.
- Equipment: ZERO documented.
- Analyst / quality control: ZERO documented — these job titles did not meaningfully exist in 1991 college football, so their absence is expected rather than a gap.
- Video coordinator, academic support, student assistants: ZERO documented.
- Assistant strength coaches under Brad Roll: ZERO documented.

SEARCH PATHS EXHAUSTED (all failed, so you know not to re-try them):
1. Wayback Machine / school athletics staff directory: STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE for this title. The championship was won January 1, 1992; the Wayback Machine's earliest captures date to 1996, and miamihurricanes.com did not exist in 1991-92. There is no archived contemporaneous staff directory to retrieve.
2. Media guide: NOT AVAILABLE. archive.org holds Miami football media guides for 1976, 1984 (plus a 1984 Orange Bowl guide), 1988, then nothing until 2006 — no 1991 or 1992 guide. The University of Miami's own digital collections (digitalcollections.library.miami.edu) return no football media guides at all. No 1991/1992 Miami guide found on issuu.
3. Official school site: miamihurricanes.com does publish a 1991-92 football roster page (https://miamihurricanes.com/sports/football/roster/season/1991-92/), but its "Coaching Staff" tab is EMPTY for that season — the page contains only players, and zero coach names appear anywhere in the page source. It is useless as a staff source.
4. Contemporary news: searches for 1991 Miami trainer / equipment manager / football operations returned nothing. Full-text search of UM's digitized student newspaper (The Miami Hurricane) for football support-staff terms returned only pre-1984 hits.

DATA CAVEATS TO CARRY FORWARD:
- Two men are documented as "defensive line" coach on the same 1991 staff (Bob Karmelowicz and Ed Orgeron). Both citations are solid and independent; period practice was likely a DE/DT split, but no source I found states the division. Neither should be dropped as a duplicate.
- Jim Michalczik's role wording conflicts between sources: Wikipedia's infobox lists him as "1990–1991 Miami (FL) (DL)" while State of The U calls him one of Erickson's GAs. I categorized him gradasst per the source that speaks directly about the 1991 staff, but the on-field/GA boundary for him is genuinely ambiguous.
- No midseason_note applies to anyone: all 14 were on staff through the January 1, 1992 Orange Bowl. Ed Orgeron's well-known leave of absence from Miami came in October 1992, a season LATER, and does not affect his 1991 ring.
- Wikipedia quotes drawn from the season page's "Coaching staff" wikitable are rendered here as the row's cell text joined by single spaces (Name Position Seasons "Alma mater"). If your matcher pipes table cells differently, fall back to the State of The U prose quote attached to the same person — every on-field coach except Bob Karmelowicz has one, and Karmelowicz has a full prose sentence from commanders.com.
